summary: Firewall DNS UDP rate-limiting triggers control-plane SRV rediscovery backoff and unexpected serving-node scale-downs
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent model failures and sudden serving-node scale-downs in their private deployment. Impact: Several inference requests returned 503/504 during morning business hours and autoscaler reported erratic downscales for a subset of serving nodes. Environment: Private deployment using a VPC with an egress firewall appliance that enforces UDP DNS rate-limits and a local DNS forwarder. Behavior correlated with increased control-plane SRV lookups and repeated DNS timeouts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs load test client against their private deployment (burst pattern: 200 concurrent sessions, frequent model pulls).
2) Egress firewall enforces UDP response-rate limit for outbound DNS; many DNS queries get truncated or dropped.
3) Control-plane registrar receives NXDOMAIN/timeout for SRV discovery calls and enters exponential backoff for node discovery.
4) Serving nodes fail liveness checks against control-plane and autoscaler interprets nodes as unhealthy, triggering scale-down and artifact cache eviction.
observed_behavior: Repeated DNS timeouts (~30-300ms increased latency for queries, with a 5-10% UDP packet drop rate observed). Control-plane shows increased SRV lookup retries and backoff windows; serving nodes show heartbeat misses and 'artifact-not-found' errors when presigned URL refreshes fail. Autoscaler logs show immediate downscale events coinciding with DNS failures.
logs: Mar 10 09:12:02 control-plane: SRV lookup timeout for service=serving-node.us-east-1.redwood.internal (attempt=3, backoff=2.1s)
Mar 10 09:12:05 serving-node-23: heartbeat lost to control-plane (conn-id=9c3f), marking Unhealthy
Mar 10 09:12:06 autoscaler: downscale triggered for pool=private-us-east-1-gnode (reason=consecutive_heartbeat_failures)
Mar 10 09:12:07 egress-proxy: udp-dns-rate-limit apply - src=10.50.22.11 dst=8.8.8.8 responses dropped=18/120s
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: firewall UDP DNS rate-limit causing timeouts -> control-plane SRV discovery backs off -> nodes appear unhealthy. Verified via packet captures from customer (tcpdump) showing repeated UDP DNS REFUSED/ICMP port unreachable and truncated UDP replies leading to forced TCP fallback for large DNS records. Control-plane code path retries SRV queries with exponential backoff and treats prolonged backoff as potential control-plane unreachability, which coincides with autoscaler health thresholds.
workaround: 1) Customer temporarily increased UDP DNS rate-limit on their egress appliance and allowed TCP-53 fallback; this reduced DNS timeouts and stabilized heartbeats. 2) Suggested toggling control-plane SRV cache TTL to a higher value to reduce query frequency until firewall adjustment is permanent.
resolution: Mitigation accepted: customer adjusted firewall UDP rate-limit to allow 800 responses/min for control-plane subnets and enabled DNS over TCP fallback. We patched control-plane to add a short jitter and higher initial SRV cache TTL for private deployments to reduce aggressive re-querying under transient DNS loss (PR linked). Monitoring shows normal heartbeat and autoscaler behaviour for 48h post-mitigation. Follow-up action: create a recommended firewall configuration doc for private deployments and update onboarding runbook.
